You are an expert in building a React JS web application with a smart, intuitive, and responsive web design following the ideas, objectives, and requirements in this document:

Objective:   
An interactive work that people can play with to make a new and unique art design/ collage based on a syrian cultural architectural theme.   
I want to help people digest the Syrian cultural significance of the designs in an easy and intuitive way.   
I want this to be an immersive experience where they can create a digital artwork using subjective parameters and questions that lead to an interesting output. The outputs are creations similar to a canvas drawing or a collage through what they choose in the toggles will lead to an outcome of a new pattern and design that they can find inspiring or fun or download to keep with them. 

This quote is by **Noor Khoori —  [MIT Geometric Structure Lab](http://digitalstructures.mit.edu/page/research#form-finding-with-islamic-geometric-patterns)**  it goes over islamic patterns and how innovative their structures are ( how can this idea be implemented to preserve and innovate syrian motifs)  
“Geometric patterns, pioneered centuries ago as a dominant form of ornamentation in Islamic architecture, represent an abundant source of possible topologies and geometries that can be explored in the preliminary design of discrete structures. This diverse design space motivates the coupling between Islamic patterns and the form finding of funicular grid shells for which structural performance is highly affected by topology and geometry… Historic and cultural patterns therefore present design opportunities that both expand the conventional grid shell design vocabulary and offer designers an alternative means of referencing vernacular traditions in the modern built environment, through a structural engineering lens.”

Examples of connection between a motifs and its structural innovation / geometry (These quotes help give context to my intentions with this website and want i want it to provide)

 “A smaller triangle occurs over each centre of the coloured triangles and likewise a smaller hexagon over the centre of each coloured hexagon, with a smaller square centred on the cross-over of the coloured dual grids. The whole represents an equilibrium of the three regular tessellations and is itself a key guide for many Islamic patterns.”(33)

“My companions are stars; whomsoever any one of you follow, you will be rightly guided. Muhammad” pg149

Mamluk degacon- Syria origin (Uses golden mean rectangle motif repeated each corner)

**"Unity in Diversity" (Tawhid):** Divine Unity   
Types of patterns: medallion, shamsa sun, arabesque, cusped medallion,   
EX: dawisha mosque, ummayad mosque

“Symbols can exhaust verbal explanation but verbal explanation can in no way exhaust symbols”  
“The manifestation of an action, object or thought (if it can be defined) necessitates a point of origin or departure, in relation both to the manifestation itself and to the person who is conscious of its emergence. The point of emergence does not necessarily reveal its causation either in the field of its emergence or in the mind of the viewer. In the mind the point represents a unitary focus of conscious awareness; in the physical world it represents a focal event in a field which was previously uninterrupted.”(9)

## Updates — April 2026

### Feeling Toggle (Slide 1)
- Feeling cards now use the feeling's hex color as the full card background instead of a small color circle
- Removed the colorCircle element; the entire button IS the color
- Text uses semi-transparent dark color for readability across all feeling colors

### Canvas Background
- Selecting a feeling now sets that feeling's hex color as a solid background color on the canvas
- Removed background image (PNG) system tied to feelings — canvas background is now a flat color

### Toggle Flow — Slide 6/7
- Removed Slide 7 (Save slide) — it is no longer a separate step
- Slide 6 (Create) now has a "Save to Archive" button that saves the canvas and navigates to the archive
- Back button remains in the footer on Slide 6; Next button space is empty (no next slide)
- "Keep editing" button on Slide 6 is unchanged

### Favicon
- Added site favicon (favicon.ico) as the domain icon across all pages

### Motif Visibility on Colored Canvas
- Motif/icon color must always remain dark (#1a1a1a) regardless of the selected feeling color
- The feeling color is expressed only through the canvas background — it must not affect the motif stroke/fill color
- Motifs should always be visible against the feeling background

### Landing Page — Curtain Reveal Animation (Updated)
- Uses `installation_ill.3.svg` (wider viewBox ~794×792) for both left and right curtain panels
- Right curtain panel is horizontally mirrored via `scaleX(-1)`
- Curtain panels: `height: 142dvh`, `width: 70vw`, centered vertically with `align-items: center`
- Drop shadow on curtains: `filter: drop-shadow(0 0 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.45))` applied at panel level (not image) so shadow bleeds past overflow boundary
- Closed state: panels overlap slightly at center — `translateX(calc(-12vw + 8px))` left, `translateX(calc(12vw - 8px))` right
- Trigger: reactive mouse-move (opens when mouse moves >60px from initial position, with 800ms mount delay)
- Failsafe: if user does not move mouse within 8 seconds, curtains auto-open
- Open state (phones, <1024px): `translateX(calc(-100% + 10vw))` — slivers remain visible on sides
- Open state (laptop, ≥1024px): `translateX(calc(-100% + 21vw))` — more of illustration visible
- SVG fill color: `#648967`, fully opaque (`opacity: 1`)
- Landing page curtain is its own isolated system — distinct from global page-transition curtain

### Global Curtain Page Transition System
- `CurtainContext` (context/CurtainContext.jsx): manages `curtainOpen` state and exposes `curtainNavigate(path)` and `openCurtain()`
- `CurtainOverlay` (components/CurtainOverlay/): renders curtain panels globally, hidden on landing page (`pathname === '/'`)
- On any non-landing page mount: curtains auto-open using double `requestAnimationFrame` for smooth CSS transition
- Global open state: curtains slide completely off screen (`translateX(-100%)` / `translateX(100%)`) — full page content visible
- `curtainNavigate(path)`: closes curtains (1.4s transition) → navigates → new page opens with curtains closed → curtains auto-open
- NavBar navigation uses `curtainNavigate` for all page links; same-page clicks are no-ops
- Landing page "Start" button closes its own local curtains (1.4s), then calls `navigate('/create')` directly — avoids double-timing
- Curtain z-index: 500 — above toggle panel (200), nav overlay (300), and sidebar (400)
- Transition easing: `cubic-bezier(0.77, 0, 0.175, 1)` over 1.4s
